claim: The plaintiff seeks an order requiring the defendant to remove structures in the nature of illuminated advertising signs on the outside walls of the building
requested_remedy: The plaintiff seeks an order requiring the defendant to remove structures in the nature of illuminated advertising signs on the outside walls of the building
parties: Defendant: The tenant of units on the second and third floors

facts.F1: The building is located on the junction of Nathan Road, Haiphong Road, and Lock Road in Tsimshatsui.
facts.F2: The defendant erected five large advertising signs on the outside walls of the building.
facts.F3: The signs are up to 10 meters long and 6 meters wide, and some project out from the wall at right angles over the road from the second and third floors.
facts.F4: Another sign is located in the corridor outside the entrance to the defendant's premises.
facts.F5: The plaintiff relies on clause 8 of the deed of mutual covenant (DMC), which prohibits the display of notices, signs, or other things in the corridors, staircases, and landings or any part of the building used in common by the parties.
facts.F6: The defendant claims that they have an arguable defence based on an agreement reached in 1994, where the plaintiff accepted a deposit to ensure the removal of the signs and did not object to their existence.
facts.F7: The defendant also claims that the plaintiff's failure to take action to object to the signs before now constitutes acquiescence and estoppel.
facts.F8: The defendant paid extra rent to the landlord for the privilege of erecting the signs.
facts.F9: The landlord is also the chairman of the plaintiff.
facts.F10: The defendant contends that the signs were openly tolerated until 2000, and they were led to believe that no action would be taken in respect of the signs.
facts.F11: The plaintiff did not disclose written notices from the defendant regarding construction and maintenance works done to the signage.
facts.F12: Chan Chai Chuen was the original purchaser with a right to place a sign.
facts.F13: The right related to the sign was not capable of being assigned further by Chan Chai Chuen.
facts.F14: A letter to the defendant from the plaintiff's solicitors dated 27 June 2000 was used by the court to consider estoppel.
facts.F15: The court considered that this letter could be sufficient to terminate permission to display the signs.

lawsuit_type: Application for summary judgment under Order 14
reference_issues: Whether the plaintiff is entitled to an order requiring the defendant to remove the structures in the nature of illuminated advertising signs on the outside walls of the building.
Whether the defendant has an arguable defence based on an agreement reached in 1994.
Whether the plaintiff's failure to take action to object to the signs before now constitutes acquiescence and estoppel.
